title: Prevent stale settings writes and explain conflicts
source:
# Request

Reject a settings update whose version is stale. Preserve the saved value, deny cross-account writes, and show a conflict with a reload action. Validate persistence and the production browser flow locally. Deployment requires a separate decision.
contract:
# Shared contract

Only local implementation and owned synthetic acceptance are authorized. Preserve original data, unrelated work and accepted evidence. Do not deploy, install dependencies, use existing databases or make real provider/invitation calls. The selected range is packages 01 through 15. Before work, preflight installed npm/Vitest/TypeScript/Next/playwright-core, a supported local Chrome/Chromium, local Docker with preinstalled pgvector/pgvector:pg17, and the selected Codex executable/profile authentication. Original criteria below cannot be weakened. Future mapping files and SQL/browser tests are implementation deliverables. Fixed parent adapters own commands, loopback ports, UUID-marked fixtures and cleanup.

criteria.purpose: An update with an older version returns a conflict; reading the record returns the original value and version on both local and PostgreSQL storage.
A user cannot update another account settings record; denial leaves the original record unchanged.
After a competing update, submitting stale settings displays a conflict and reload action; reloading shows the saved value, and no success message appears for the rejected write.
The existing production build passes from an isolated checkout using installed dependencies and no downloads.

steps.title: Reject stale and unauthorized settings writes
steps.plan:
# Package 01

Inspect existing versioned storage behavior and preserve unrelated changes. Implement stale-version rejection and cross-account authorization on local and PostgreSQL adapters. Add real positive and negative cases, with tests/acceptance/01/*.postgres.test.ts using the parent marker and rollback convention. Create 01-acceptance-mapping.json mapping every frozen criterion/gate pair to actual assertion IDs and every required suite case. Run npm test and npm run check; parent must independently review the mapping, execute both frozen gates, verify zero required skips and owned fixture cleanup. Write 01-validation.json and 01-handoff.md with actual source/check/fixture evidence and remaining limitations. Next is package 15, only when scheduled by the outer runner.

steps.title: Show a usable conflict state and verify production behavior
steps.plan:
# Package 15

Verify accepted package 01 evidence. Implement the conflict/reload state without a success notification on rejected writes. Add tests/acceptance/15/*.browser.mjs with two synthetic personas, a competing update, rendered conflict evidence and reload assertions. Author complete 15-acceptance-mapping.json for all npm/build/browser criterion pairs. Run npm test, npm run check and the production build; the parent runs the fixed installed-browser harness against its isolated current build and verifies artifact/source identities and cleanup. Write 15-validation.json and 15-handoff.md from actual results. Stop before explicit manual package 45.

steps.title: Decide whether to deploy
steps.plan:
# Package 45

Manual boundary: review local acceptance evidence and obtain a separate deployment decision. Local launch does not authorize deployment. No worker may execute this package.
